audit_findings.title: Qorvo closing would invalidate both the earnings perimeter and share denominator
audit_findings.magnitude: Qorvo holders would own approximately 37% of the combined company; consideration is 0.960 SWKS share plus $32.50 cash per Qorvo share; up to $1.5 billion of bridge financing and $1.55 billion of Qorvo notes are implicated
audit_findings.mechanism: Closing changes OE, growth assumptions, diluted shares, cash, debt, interest expense, and the equity bridge simultaneously.
audit_findings.evidence: Under the terms of the Merger Agreement, at the effective time of the Mergers, each share of Qorvo common stock issued and outstanding immediately prior thereto (with certain exceptions set forth in the Merger Agreement) will be converted into the right to receive 0.960 (the “Exchange Ratio”) of a share of Skyworks common stock and $ 32.50 in cash, without interest, subject to applicable withholding taxes.
audit_findings.explanation: This is not an error in the explicitly standalone, as-filed valuation while the transaction remains pending. It is a forward-looking perimeter change that would make every present scenario non-comparable with the post-closing company. The direction cannot be determined without Qorvo owner earnings, financing terms, integration costs, and synergies.
audit_findings.action: Confirm transaction status before relying on the valuation. Upon closing, rerun with actual shares issued, Qorvo operating results, cash paid, assumed and newly issued debt, financing costs, purchase accounting, integration spending, and any required divestitures.

audit_findings.title: A contingent Singapore tax clawback may be an unmodeled claim ahead of common equity
audit_findings.magnitude: potential clawback up to $336.4 million, equal to $2.13 per valuation share and 3.6% of the $9.279 billion base equity value; future tax-rate effect unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: A refund would reduce the cash bridge, while early loss or scheduled expiration of the concession would reduce future after-tax OE and terminal value.
audit_findings.evidence: If we cannot, or elect not to, comply with the conditions for the tax holiday, we could be required to refund certain previously realized tax benefits for fiscal years 2021 through 2025, over which period we enjoyed a tax holiday that decreased our taxes by a cumulative $336.4 million, and we may lose the benefits of the tax holiday earlier than scheduled.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates the size of benefits potentially subject to refund but does not establish that a refund is probable or quantify the recurring post-concession tax burden. The $336.4 million clawback alone would not reverse the current conclusion because adjusted bull value would remain about $66.24 per share versus the $74.02 price. The unquantified recurring tax-rate effect could be more important because it would affect forecast and terminal OE.
audit_findings.action: Obtain current compliance evidence for employment and investment thresholds, identify any related accrual in the latest accounts, and rerun all scenarios using the expected tax rate through and after September 2030 plus any probable refund.

audit_findings.title: The gross cash bridge may omit an already-accrued repatriation-tax claim
audit_findings.magnitude: no more than the latest filed $68.7 million total accrued-taxes balance, or $0.43 per valuation share and 0.74% of the $9.279 billion base equity value; the prior specific balance was $56.3 million
audit_findings.mechanism: Any unpaid non-operating repatriation tax should reduce the $799.2 million cash and short-term-investment bridge because the associated tax expense was already recognized.
audit_findings.evidence: The Company had accrued $ 56.3 million of the deemed repatriation tax in short-term liabilities within the Consolidated Balance Sheets as of October 3, 2025.
audit_findings.explanation: The latest filing does not separately identify the remaining repatriation-tax balance, so the specific omission is unresolved. Nevertheless, the entire latest accrued-taxes balance provides a filed upper bound: deducting $68.7 million would reduce base value from $58.70 to about $58.27 per share and bull value from $68.37 to about $67.94, leaving the valuation conclusion unchanged relative to the $74.02 price.
audit_findings.action: Inspect the July 2026 tax-liability roll-forward or obtain management confirmation of the unpaid repatriation-tax balance; deduct any confirmed non-operating amount from the cash bridge in the next rerun.

audit_findings.title: Mandatory Singapore factory relocation may require capital spending above historical maintenance needs
audit_findings.mechanism: Incremental construction, equipment transfer, duplicate operations, qualification, and disruption costs would reduce explicit-period OE or require a separate equity-value deduction.
audit_findings.evidence: Because the owner of the site for our Singapore Filter Manufacturing Facility has decided to redevelop it for other uses, we will need to relocate our Singapore Filter Manufacturing Facility by the end of the sublease, and we have been exploring alternative sites in other locations.
audit_findings.explanation: Relocation by July 2030 is a filed requirement, but no relocation budget or committed incremental spending is supplied. Singapore property, plant, and equipment was $215.0 million at fiscal 2025 year-end, providing scale context but not a valid estimate of relocation cost. Because the spending is forward-looking and cannot yet be separated from ordinary maintenance or growth capital, its present materiality cannot be quantified.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the approved site plan, gross and incentive-net capital budget, equipment-transfer schedule, duplicate-running costs, expected downtime, and amounts already included in ordinary capex; rerun OE when committed amounts become available.

audit_findings.title: Denso litigation presents an unaccrued damages and injunction tail risk
audit_findings.magnitude: unquantified settled charge; zero remaining Denso litigation tail
audit_findings.mechanism: Before settlement, damages would have reduced the equity bridge or OE and an injunction could have reduced future OE; settlement removes those prospective mechanisms.
audit_findings.evidence: Denso is seeking monetary damages, including enhanced damages, interest, fees and costs, and injunctive relief.
audit_findings.explanation: The latest 10-Q states that the Denso litigation was settled during the nine months ended July 3, 2026 and that the recognized charge was immaterial. Consequently, the supplied damages-and-injunction tail no longer exists: remaining exposure from this case is zero compared with the $9.279 billion base equity value. The undisclosed settlement charge is a fiscal 2026 one-time item rather than a recurring reduction in normalized OE.
audit_findings.action: Confirm that the settlement fully released all U.S. and Japanese claims and identify the cash paid only for bridge reconciliation; no recurring valuation adjustment is needed absent continuing royalties or licensing obligations.

audit_findings.title: The FY2025 anchor contains an extra operating week
audit_findings.magnitude: simple 52-week normalization reduces anchor OE by $12.0 million, from $637.9 million to $625.9 million; base operating PV falls approximately $160.0 million or $1.01 per share
audit_findings.mechanism: The extra week overstates recurring anchor OE and therefore every explicit forecast cash flow and terminal value derived from that anchor.
audit_findings.evidence: The fiscal year ended on October 3, 2025 (“fiscal 2025”) consisted of 53 weeks.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated calendar-normalization error. A simple 52/53 adjustment lowers the anchor by 1.89%. Applying the same proportion to base operating PV reduces base value from $58.70 to approximately $57.69 per share; bull value would fall by approximately $1.19 to $67.18. All remain below the $74.02 market price, so the valuation conclusion is unchanged.
audit_findings.action: Replace the anchor with a 52-week normalized figure, preferably using actual revenue, margins, working capital, and capex attributable to the extra week; otherwise use the transparent $625.9 million pro-rata anchor and rerun all scenarios.
